name: Basingstoke and Deane

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme; only national mandatory HMO licensing applies (five or more people from two or more households). Separately, an Article 4 direction means converting a house to an HMO needs planning permission in Basingstoke town, Chineham, Old Basing, Oakley and Sherborne St John.
licensing.fee: £489 on application plus £619 on grant for a new HMO licence (2026/27 fees)

privateRentedShare.text: 15.4% of households rent privately (Census 2021), up from 11.8% in 2011

councilTax.text: £2,225 Band D (2026/27) where there is no parish council, including Hampshire County Council, police and fire (about £2,255 on average with parish precepts)

housing: Basingstoke grew rapidly as a London overspill town from the 1960s, so much of its housing is planned estates of terraced and semi-detached houses, with newer estates and apartment blocks on the edges and near the station. The rest of the borough is rural north Hampshire, with villages of brick and flint cottages. Private rented homes are mostly in the town’s estates and flats, let to commuters and people working locally.
checkinTips: 1960s–1980s estate houses: photograph flat-roofed porches and garages, uPVC windows and doors, and the number of keys and garage fobs.
Apartment blocks near Basingstoke station: note fob, key and parking permit counts, and photograph the meter cupboard and bin store.
Brick and flint cottages in the villages: photograph walls and window reveals for damp, and any open fire or stove with its hearth.
Rural homes off mains gas: photograph oil tanks and the gauge reading, and the cover of any septic tank or treatment plant.
New-build homes: photograph sealant around baths and showers, settlement cracks in plaster and the state of turfed gardens.
tenantHelp: Tenants in Basingstoke and Deane can contact the borough council’s private sector housing team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in a rented home.
